December 2009 # Sentimental market - Refined production will continue to improve to take advantage of prices well above the costs of most mines, as there have been few supply disruptions and the Spence strike is now over. - Chinese imports and apparent consumption continue to decline from the June highs, showing the market is oversupplied. Real demand, however, remains robust. With growth struggling to gain momentum in the rest of the world, exchange stocks are therefore seeing an influx of metal and should soon hit a new high for this year. - LME prices have also hit a new 2009 high, as investors appear to be positioning themselves well ahead of the fundamentals. We expect a correction soon but would not be surprised if sentiment, movements in the US dollar and investment inflows do not combine to push prices higher, possibly testing upside resistance at $7,125/t. |The supply/demand

# China remains the key Last month we identified the Chinese stocking situation as **LME price ($/t)** the swing factor that should direct copper pricing. This is **9000** still the case. Real copper demand remains robust in **8000** China and we estimate growth will be about 13% y-o-y in Q4 as a whole, as semis production growth is sustained at **7000** a high level due to strong industrial production growth generally. In contrast, Chinese apparent consumption and **6000** imports of refined copper are in decline. In addition, exchange stocks globally have risen again to over **5000** 600,000t and are rapidly approaching a new 2009 high, thus confirming the weakness of demand outside of **4000** China. A combination of rising exchange stocks and **3000** falling Chinese imports would normally lead to lower **Cash Price** prices. Instead, copper prices on the LME have **LME Stocks 2000** maintained the upward trend which began at the **01-08 04-08 07-08 10-08 12-08 04-09 07-09** beginning of October, with 3-month prices touching a Data: LME high of $7,020/t on 25th November. Positive sentiment about the prospects for economic recovery is driving investment flows into commodities, including copper, as investors position themselves well ahead of the fundamentals. One consequence of the recovery in copper prices has also been a mini-boom in the buying and selling of marginal copper assets, particularly in Africa. While not massive, these deals amount to over US$1.3M. In addition, there has been an increase in IPOs among Australian juniors. Both developments are further evidence of a return of appetite for risk, as well as reflection of increased liquidity. Even when the strength of the economic recovery is thrown into doubt – as with the news that US GDP growth in Q3 had been revised down to only 2.8% from 3.5% – the market appears to be largely shrugging this off. The question remains – Is the flow of money into commodities, including copper, going to be sustained? Or will the weak market fundamentals reassert themselves? Developments in Chinese cathode and scrap China will remain key. Congestion at customs in August seems to be the reason behind the surprisingly high refined imports recorded in September. Therefore, the fall m-o-m in October imports is overstated when looked at on a percentage basis (down 40%), as imports of just under 170,0

00t are high by historical standards. Nevertheless, October imports were over 40,000t below the monthly average of 210,000t/m that we estimate are required to balance the Chinese market. Refined cathode exports also jumped to almost 20,000t in October, the highest level since August 2008. Therefore, we estimate that apparent consumption in China was 529,000t in October, down by almost 175,000t since peaking in June, and reflects the soft offtake in the spot market in China. In a further confirmation of the oversupply in the country, Chinese imports of scrap fell below 100,000t (on a 35% contained metal basis) for the first time since the extreme lows hit in January and February. The decline in apparent consumption in China is in line with our view that Data: CRU Analysis the Chinese market has over 700,000t of spare copper in the hands of traders and speculative players in the country. The table above shows our estimates of the breakdown of the stock build in China. We believe that the SRB sold back some of the material it bought earlier in the year, leaving a net build of 160,000t in its warehouses. A further 260,000t can be accounted for by stocking/restocking at semis fabricators and a build up of inventory at refined cathode producers. In addition, our China consultant estimates that there is some 150,000t in bonded warehouses in Shanghai and a further 200,000t elsewhere in the country, with most of this believed to be in the hands of traders. We believe that 200-300,000t of the remaining 370,000t is owned by other traders and speculative players, such as the proverbial “pig farmer”. The latter is not just the figment of journalists‟ overactive imaginations, but does actually exist, according to reports from some of our contacts. However, these are relatively rich people who took a punt on the low copper (and nickel) prices earlier this year. The question is “How much of the material held in bonded warehouses and by the speculative players will be released to the market and at what price?” One clue comes from the spot premium for imported cathode into China. If speculators were releasing material into the market w

e would have expected premiums to fall further.  Nevertheless, the premium has stabilised at about $50/t over the past two months.  As prices keep rising, we believe they will hold off selling until some time next year and we do not expect monthly cathode exports from China to increase from the level seen in October. 

## **Recovery in demand in the world excluding China remains subdued** 

There has been only one change in the overall demand picture for refined copper in the world excluding China since the last monitor.  We have confirmed an increase in orders for cathode from the semis industry in northern Europe, after the summer shutdowns.  Demand, however, has softened again in recent weeks.  The recovery in southern Europe is lagging that in the north, as end-use demand itself is poor.  In the USA, semis production is flatlining and spot demand for cathode is reported as “dead”.  In the rest of Asia, the restocking phase seen in Q2 appears to have largely run its course, leaving sequential growth in demand for cathode rising at a more modest rate of 3.2% q-o-q in the fourth quarter. 

The real risk to demand in the world excluding China at the moment is the possibility of economic policy missteps.  Politicians appear to be taking asset price recoveries, such as that of copper and equities, as a sign of the end of the economic crisis and many have begun talking of tackling high government debt levels.  However, unemployment continues to rise and will be a drag on consumer spending, while the banking systems in most countries remain fragile.  For example, 23% of US home loans are in negative equity and banks are potentially exposed to another round of pain from residential mortgage write downs. Hence, the ability of the private sector to take over from government stimulus as the driver of economic growth appears limited, especially in the developed world.

## **Spot premiums steady, 2010 annual contracts few and far between** 

Premiums for spot cathode sales have been flat m-o-m, as physical supply is generally plentiful everywhere, with premiums in the USA unchanged at 3.5-4.5¢/lb and those in Europe widening on the downside to $40-70/t. 

Codelco is in the middle of negotiating annual contracts with Chinese customers.  A headline annual premium of $85/t has been announced, following agreement of a $75/t premium for Japan, $74/t for Korea and a steady $80/t for European customers.   However, what we hear is that there is little enthusiasm among consumers to confirm volumes for next year.  With stocks plentiful and rising (at least on exchanges) this is not irrational.  We expect that there will be few deals agreed until mid-December, with many customers dragging out negotiations into the New Year. 

## **Stock movements confirm weak demand** 

The recent push to a new annual high for prices has come despite exchange stocks glo

bally rising to over 600,000t and being on course to hit a new 2009 high as well.  The rise in stocks so far in November has been at a rate of 4,775t per day, the fastest pace since the run up in stocks in late January and February. The difference from earlier this year is the location of the stocks and the pace of the increase.  Unlike in January, when Europe was the leading destination for surplus stocks, LME stocks in the region have risen by only 16,000t since hitting a low in August of 62,000t.  What may have happened is that material that would have gone into Europe has instead flowed to the USA and Asia.  Some possibly has gone to Comex, to take advantage of the sustained arbitrage.  As for Asia, exchange stocks (LME+SHFE) fell to a low of just 6% of total exchange stocks in April, as Chinese imports rose and pulled material out of LME warehouses.  Since then, as Chinese imports slowed, Asian exchange stocks have recovered to make up 1/3 of total exchange stocks.  Furthermore, the recent pick up in Chinese exports saw most of this metal head to South Korea and Singapore and likely into the LME warehouses. 

## **Supply side pressures limited** 

Strikes and the threat of strikes in South America are the main supply-side story at the moment, as there have been no reports of significant disruptions to production elsewhere.  Many major mines in Chile have come to agreement with unions on new labour agreements without disruption, the latest being BHPBilliton‟s Cerro Colorado.  The only exception had been Spence.  The strike has been resolved this week after a 42day walkout, which was the longest mining strike in Chile for many decades, if not the longest ever.  This is the first renewal of the Spence collective labour agreement.  The difficult labour negotiations extend back to the opening of the mine in 2006, when workers went on strike for higher pay even before the mine had opened.  The striking employees at Spence were reported to have allegedly entered the mine and vandalised some equipment, but BHPBilliton expects to be back to full capacity by mid-January 2010. 

The only remaining significant labour contracts are at Antamina in Peru and Chuquicamata in Chile.  The previous agreement is still in place at Antamina despite coming to an end in July.   The negotiations at Chuquicamata could get caught up in the Presidential elections, which take place on 13th December 2009. So if these two negotiations do not run smoothly there could still be further supply disruptions before the year is out. 

## **Prices should see a correction, but uncertainty remains high** 

The underlying short term fundamentals remain poor for copper.  Therefore, we expect prices to test downside support sometime soon.  Technical indicators in CRU‟s November _LME metals – technical analysis_ report are currently pointing to $6,600/t as the likely support level.  However, copper and other commodities are being strongly influenced by sentiment, movements in the US doll

t **BHP Billiton’s Spence** mine in Chile voted to end a 42-day strike (the longest held in Chile) and the new agreement (4% wage increase during the duration of the 41-month collective contract) was signed on 25<sup>th</sup> November.  BHP Billiton expect to return to normal production by mid-January, according to media reports.  The negotiations had been tense between the workers and the company.  On the 37<sup>th</sup> day of the stoppage strikers invaded the site and employees were evacuated.  In 2009, CRU expects Spence to produce 165,000t of EW copper cathode. 

- **BHP Billiton’s** management made an early offer to the unionised workers at **Cerro Colorado** , where the collective labour agreement expires on 31<sup>st</sup> January 2010.  Unionised workers at Cerro Colorado accepted the offer of single 4.8% wage increase and a bonus of US$20,000 per worker for a 41month collective contract.  In 2009, Cerro Colorado is expected to produce 150,000t of EW copper cathode. 

- Unionised workers at **Codelco’s Chuquicamata** mine in Chile asked for a 7.5% salary increase in their new 30-month collective labour contract.  Elsewhere, on 22<sup>nd</sup> November, workers at Codelco‟s **Andina** mine have agreed to a single 3.0% wage increase, around US$14,000 in bonuses and benefits, and around US$5,000 in soft loans.  In 2009, CRU expects Chuquicamata to produce 320,000t of copper-in-concentrates and 125,000t of EW cathode, and Andina to produce 218,000t of copper-in-concentrate. 

- Negotiations between the management and the union at **Antamina** in Peru (jointly owned by **BHP Billiton** , **Xstrata** , **Teck** and **Mitsubishi Corporation** ) have so far failed to reach agreement on a new collective labour contract.  The previous deal expired in July and the union was threatening to go on strike.  However, according to press reports, mediation talks by the Ministry of Labour were due to be held on 17<sup>th</sup> November.  This would be the second stage of the negotiations, with the third phase being either arbitration or industrial action.  In Peru, there is no a legal limit to how long negotiations can take, in comparison to Chile where labour legislation specifies collective labour agreements and negotiations in great detail (including the timing of the start and length of strikes).  In 2009, CRU expects that Antamina will produce 315,000t of copper-in-concentrate. 

- On 16<sup>th</sup> November, **Newmont Mining** announced that its subsidiary **Newmont Indonesia Limited** , together with **NT Mining Corporation** (an affiliate of **Sumitomo Corporation** ), had completed the transfer of 10% of **PT Newmont Nusa Tengara** (PTNNT) to **PT Multi Daerah Bersaing** (PTMDB) for US$391M.  PTMDB is a consortium of local and regional governments near the **Batu Hijau** mine (Indonesia) and a private company.  The 10% stake is comprised of 3% for the 2006 divesture and 7% for the 2007 divesture.  Further, on 23<sup>rd</sup> November, it was repo

rted that a consortium of Indonesian local governments had agreed to purchase a 14% stake of PTNNT for US$493.6M.  Both transactions are part of the divestment dispute between the Indonesian government and the foreign owners of PTNNT.  Batu Hijau is expected to produce 195,000t of copper-in-concentrate in 2009. 

- It was reported that operations at **Luanshya Copper Mines** ( **LCM** )‟s **Baluba** mine (Zambia) will resume on 15<sup>th</sup> December, two weeks ahead of schedule, after the modernisation of the copper processing plant. - spent US$70M on the project.  In 2008, Baluba produced 20,000t of copper-in-concentrates and was placed on care and maintenance in December 2008. 





- In early November, the **National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration** (NOAA) announced that **El Niсo** (a disruption of the ocean-atmosphere system in the Tropical Pacific) is expected to continue strengthening and last through at least the Northern Hemisphere winter in 2009-2010.  For copper production, the effects of El Niсo have been affecting the logistics chain at **Ok Tedi** in Papua New Guinea.  In addition, as previous times, El Niсo can cause a wetter than usual rainy season in Northern Peru (likely to halt exploration activity at some promising deposits) and a dry rainy season in Southern Peru (likely to put constraints on water availability and hydro electricity generation). 

- In mid November, a US federal judge favoured the US$2.5B bid (US$2.2B in cash and US$280M in notes) of **Grupo Mexico** for **Asarco** . Grupo Mexico is currently competing for control of Asarco against **Sterlite Industries** (India), whose latest bid is US$2.565B according to press reports. 

## **Exploration and Development** 





- On 23<sup>rd</sup> November, **First Quantum Minerals** ( **FQM** ) announced that is has agreed to acquire the entire issued share capital of Kiwara Plc for a total of US$260.2M. Kiwara is an exploration and development junior mining company, with a focus on base metals in Zambian North Western Province.  Kiwara‟s operations are at an early stage of development and first drillings are taking place.  In 2009, CRU expects FQM to produce 81,000t of EW copper cathode from their operations in Zambia and the DR Congo. 

- It was reported that **Southern Copper Corporation** ( **SCC** ) said it will push back the start of its **Tia Maria** project in Arequipa (Peru) by six months towards the end of 2011.  The project requires an investment of about US$930-1,000M and currently faces problems with surrounding communities that are worried about the effects on their water supply.  Tia Maria is expected to produce 120,000t/y of EW cathode at full production. 

## **Smelting and Refining** 







- In mid-November, **Codelco** raised annual co

ntract premiums for refined copper to be delivered to China in 2010 to US$85/t (a US$10/t increase) over the London Metal Exchange cash price.  In addition, Codelco announced premiums of US$75/t on shipments to Yokohama (Japan), US$74/t on shipments to South Korea and US$80/t on shipments to Europe.  In 2009, Codelco is expected to produce 1,155,000t of electro-refined copper and 623,000t of EW copper cathode. 

- It was reported that **Yunnan Copper Group** announced that by the end of this year they will complete a 100,000t/y anode copper project at their **Kunpeng Copper Co** in Liangshan (Sichuan Province, China).  The project requires an investment of around CNY1.06B (~US$155M) and it is expected to start commissioning in March 2010. 

- On 11<sup>th</sup> and 12<sup>th</sup> November, around 1,500 workers at Zambia‟s **Konkola Copper Mines** ( **KCM** ) held a strike over wages increases.  All operations were halted, except the smelter where the process is automated.  The majority of workers resumed work on 13<sup>th</sup> November and operations are now running as usual.  Negotiations about the salary increases were about to resume as well.  In 2009, CRU expects KCM to produce 140,000t of copper blister.

## **Consumption** 



- The **US International Trade Commission** decided to continue its anti-dumping duty investigations into imports of copper seamless tube. **Luvata** said that its imports from **China** were offset by production cuts at **Luvata Franklin** and should be excluded from the petitioners‟ import data. **Johnson Controls** claimed that Chinese seamless copper tube outperforms locally produced tube in terms of quality and environmental standards. 



- According to data released by the **Japanese Electric Wire and Cable Association** , October copper wire and cable shipments in Japan fell by 14.3% y-o-y  to 61,000t.  However, the figure was up by 5.2% from September.  Only power and telecoms cable segments experienced year-on-year rises in October.  Shipments to the power industry increased by 15.6% to 8,100t.  Sales to the construction, automotive and home appliance sectors as well as export volumes contracted on an annual basis. 



- **Nissan Copper** is aiming to start production at its new copper tube plant in **Silvassa** , **India** , in June 2010.  Output capacity amounts to 12,000t per annum.  According to plans, 60% of production will be exported to the **United Arab Emirates** whilst the remaining 40% will serve domestic needs. 



- Wire and cable company **Prysmian** announced that sales in the nine months to September reached €2.8B (US$4.2B), an organic contraction of 17.5% y-o-y.  But the company said that Q3 contracted by 16% y-o-y compared to shrinkage of 18.3% in H1 2009, showing sequential improvement.  The strategic high voltage power transmission cable business saw order recovery in Q3,

with order backlogs through 2010.
